statements.text: "Congress must have strong oversight and transparency over federal AI use,” Congressman Walkinshaw said. “When intelligence agencies use AI to analyze sensitive communications and data, Congress needs to know how they use it and for what purpose. Our laws and oversight must keep pace with the technology."
statements.venue: Press release on FISA AI Reporting Act (House website)

statements.text: I think it is more critical in federal adoption that we do it responsibly, because if something goes wrong in the federal government, it’s my constituents’ data, lives, health, safety that’s at risk.

I also think it’s really important that there be a human being in the chain when decisions are made that impact people’s lives. When there are subjective decisions that need to be made to approve or deny a disability claim, a human being needs to be making that decision.

So I think really it’s incumbent upon us. We have to have real standards and regulations around AI and data centers. statements.text: I think we should have transparency around the models. There should be independent third-party review and testing, safety testing of new fronttier models before they can be released. There should be a kill switch on frontier models so if they get out of control, they can be shut off by a human. being.

statements.text: In Congress, I am pushing for data centers to cover their own energy costs, adhere to strict environmental standards, and give communities a genuine voice in siting decisions. I am also working to repeal the massive tax breaks granted to data center developers under the Big Beautiful Bill. It is also imperative that Congress regulate the advanced AI technology fueling the construction of new data centers.
